statement: The block provides PARA_NUM_REGS 32-bit read/write control registers and one 32-bit read-only status register.
The current value of every read/write register drives o_regs directly.
A read of the status register at byte address 0x40 returns the SoC status word i_status.
The block implements 1 to 16 read/write registers at byte addresses 0x00 + 4k.
Each read/write register resets to 0.
Byte-lane writes are controlled by i_s_axi_wstrb.
The status read returns i_status as sampled when the read address is taken.
An access to an unmapped address answers SLVERR.
An unmapped read returns 0.
The write address and the write data may arrive in either order or at the same edge, and the block must accept all.
A read and a write may be in progress at the same time, as the read and write paths work independently.
The write response comes one cycle after the last write handshake, and the read data one cycle after the read address handshake.
Every output is registered, with no combinational path from any input to any output.
The block uses one clock and one active-low reset with asynchronous assertion.
The block never produces response codes EXOKAY (2'b01) or DECERR (2'b11).
i_s_axi_awprot and i_s_axi_arprot are ignored.
Address bits [1:0] are ignored and no unaligned-access error is produced.
A transfer occurs at a rising edge of i_clk when valid and ready of a channel are both 1 and i_rst_n is 1; the payload is taken at that edge.
A value required 'from edge n' holds starting in cycle n+1 until another requirement changes it, such as a held state ending or a reset.

not_verified.note: Definition of 'from edge n'; used as the timing convention in all assertions (CHK-016, CHK-008, CHK-002, CHK-012).

statement: A write address, write data or read address is held in cycle n if its transfer occurred at an edge <= n-1, its B or R transfer has not occurred, and i_rst_n has not been 0 since; reset ends the held state.
PARA_NUM_REGS sets the number of read/write registers, default 8, with legal values 1 to 16.
PARA_ADDR_W sets the width in bits of i_s_axi_awaddr and i_s_axi_araddr, default 8, legal values 7 to 16.
The block must behave as the specification states for every legal combination of PARA_NUM_REGS (1 to 16) and PARA_ADDR_W (7 to 16).

not_verified.note: Parameter sweep across all legal combinations; each simulation covers one configuration, the plan is run in every configuration of section 11.

statement: LPARA_REGS_W shall be a local parameter equal to PARA_NUM_REGS*32 that cannot be overridden from outside the module.

not_verified.note: Localparam definition / not overridable is a source property (lint/elaboration).

statement: The RTL should stop elaboration with an error message when PARA_NUM_REGS or PARA_ADDR_W is outside its legal range.

not_verified.note: Elaboration error on illegal parameters; not a simulation property.

statement: Behaviour with illegal parameter values is unspecified and must not be verified.

not_verified.note: Illegal parameter values are explicitly not verified.

statement: Byte lane i of a register must be bits 8i+7..8i and correspond to i_s_axi_wdata[8i+7:8i] and o_s_axi_rdata[8i+7:8i].
Byte lane i of a register must be enabled by i_s_axi_wstrb[i].
Bits 32k+31..32k of o_regs must carry the current value of read/write register k.
Every output must change value only at a rising edge of i_clk or when i_rst_n is asserted.
The values of i_s_axi_awprot and i_s_axi_arprot must have no effect on any output.
Every flip-flop of the block shall be clocked by the rising edge of i_clk.
Every output shall take its reset value asynchronously, without waiting for a rising edge of i_clk.
o_s_axi_awready, o_s_axi_wready, o_s_axi_arready, o_s_axi_bvalid and o_s_axi_rvalid shall be 0.
o_s_axi_bresp, o_s_axi_rresp and o_s_axi_rdata shall be 0.
Every bit of o_regs shall be 0.
No transfer shall happen on any channel, whatever the values of the valid and ready inputs.
No transfer shall happen on any channel at R1, because the ready outputs and bvalid/rvalid are 0 in the cycle ending at R1.
o_s_axi_awready, o_s_axi_wready and o_s_axi_arready shall be 1.
o_s_axi_bvalid and o_s_axi_rvalid shall stay 0.
The held state shall be discarded.
No B or R response shall be given for that transaction, and no register shall be written by it.
It shall be treated as a new transfer request, taken at the first edge after R1 where the matching ready is 1.
Bits [1:0] of i_s_axi_awaddr and i_s_axi_araddr must have no effect on any output.
An address with word index k selects read/write register k.
The address selects the status register.
Every other address is unmapped.
Decode compares all address bits [PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] so no register or status register appears at more than one word index (no aliasing).
A write transaction is decoded from the address taken at its AW transfer.
A read transaction is decoded from the address taken at its AR transfer.
o_s_axi_awready shall be 1.
o_s_axi_awready shall be 0.
o_s_axi_wready shall be 1.
o_s_axi_wready shall be 0.
The block takes the AW and W transfers in either order or at the same edge.
The block shall not answer a write transaction before it has taken both AW and W transfers.
The block shall take no other AW transfer.
The block shall take no other W transfer.
The strobes and data used are the values of i_s_axi_wstrb and i_s_axi_wdata taken at the W transfer.
Bits 8i+7..8i of register k take the value of the same bits of the write data taken at Ew.
Byte lanes of register k whose strobe bit is 0 keep their value.
The written value appears on o_regs[32k+31:32k] from edge Ec, in the cycle starting at Ec.
A write shall change no bit of o_regs outside bits 32k+31..32k.
A write changes its register only at its edge Ec and only once.
The write shall change no bit of o_regs.
The write shall change no bit of o_regs.
The write changes no bit of o_regs and answers OKAY.
Bits of o_regs shall not change.
o_s_axi_bvalid shall be 1 in the cycle starting at Ec.
o_s_axi_bvalid stays 1 and o_s_axi_bresp stays unchanged.
o_s_axi_bvalid shall be 0.
The block gives exactly one B transfer per write transaction.
o_s_axi_bvalid shall be 0.
o_s_axi_bresp shall be 2'b00 (OKAY).
o_s_axi_bresp shall be 2'b10 (SLVERR).
o_s_axi_bresp shall never be 2'b01 or 2'b11.
The value of o_s_axi_bresp is unspecified and shall not be checked.
o_s_axi_arready shall be 1.
o_s_axi_arready shall be 0.
The block shall take no other AR transfer.
o_s_axi_rvalid shall be 1 in the cycle starting at Ear.
o_s_axi_rvalid stays 1 and o_s_axi_rdata and o_s_axi_rresp stay unchanged.
o_s_axi_rvalid shall be 0.
The block gives exactly one R transfer for each AR transfer.
o_s_axi_rvalid shall be 0.
o_s_axi_rdata equals o_regs[32k+31:32k] in the cycle ending at Ear.
o_s_axi_rdata equals i_status in the cycle ending at Ear.
The change shall not alter o_s_axi_rdata.
o_s_axi_rresp shall be 2'b00 (OKAY).
o_s_axi_rdata shall be 32'h0000_0000 and o_s_axi_rresp shall be 2'b10 (SLVERR).
o_s_axi_rresp shall never be 2'b01 or 2'b11.
Values of o_s_axi_rdata and o_s_axi_rresp are unspecified and shall not be checked.
A read shall change no bit of o_regs.
AR and R channels work independently of AW, W and B: value and timing of arready, rvalid, rdata, rresp are unchanged, except register value per REQ-CC-003 to 006.
The value and timing of awready, wready, bvalid, bresp and o_regs shall not change.
The read returns the old value of register k before that write.
The read returns the value written, unless another write to k with Ec before Ear came in between.
The write shall not change o_s_axi_rdata of the read.
Read data equals one whole value register k held in the cycle ending at Ear, never a mix of bytes of two values.
The block completes one write transaction every 2 cycles: AW and W transfers at edge n, B transfer at edge n+1, next AW and W at edge n+2.
The block completes one read transaction every 2 cycles: AR transfer at edge n, R transfer at edge n+1, next AR at edge n+2.
The block's readies must not wait for the matching valid; o_s_axi_awready, o_s_axi_wready and o_s_axi_arready are 1 as REQ-WR-001, REQ-WR-003 and REQ-RD-001 say, regardless of the valids.
The block keeps the write response pending for any number of cycles while i_s_axi_bready is 0.
The block takes no new AW or W transfer while the B response is pending and i_s_axi_bready is 0.
The block keeps the read data pending for any number of cycles while i_s_axi_rready is 0.
The block takes no new AR transfer while read data is pending and i_s_axi_rready is 0.
Back-pressure on the B channel must not stall the AR or R channel.
Back-pressure on the R channel must not stall the AW, W or B channel.
The block answers write transactions in the order of their Ec and read transactions in the order of their Ear.
REG_k VALUE (bits 31:0, RW) shall reset to 0x0000_0000, so o_regs[32k+31:32k] is 0 after reset.
o_regs[32k+31:32k] shall be driven by the current value of REG_k.
Each byte lane of REG_k shall be written only when the corresponding i_s_axi_wstrb bit is set; other byte lanes shall keep their value.
A read of REG_k shall return the current register value with OKAY response.
A read of STATUS shall return i_status sampled at Ear, with OKAY response.
A write to STATUS shall change nothing and answer OKAY.
A read of the unmapped region below STATUS shall return 0 with SLVERR.
A write to the unmapped region below STATUS shall change nothing and answer SLVERR.
The reserved region from 4*PARA_NUM_REGS to 0x3C shall not exist when PARA_NUM_REGS is 16.
A read of the unmapped region above STATUS shall return 0 with SLVERR.
A write to the unmapped region above STATUS shall change nothing and answer SLVERR.
Address bits [1:0] shall be ignored when decoding register offsets.
The register map shall match the table exactly for every legal PARA_NUM_REGS and PARA_ADDR_W combination.
A write to an unmapped address, detected by decoding the address taken at Ea, must change no register and answer o_s_axi_bresp = 2'b10 (SLVERR) with normal write timing.
A read from an unmapped address, detected by decoding the address taken at Ear, must return o_s_axi_rdata = 0 and o_s_axi_rresp = 2'b10 (SLVERR) with normal read timing.
A write to the status register must change no register, not affect later status reads other than through i_status, and answer OKAY, for every i_s_axi_wstrb value.
A write with i_s_axi_wstrb = 4'b0000 must answer as a write with strobes to the same address (OKAY for register or status, SLVERR for unmapped) and change no register.
An address with bits [1:0] not equal to 2'b00 must not be treated as an error.
An access with unaligned address bits [1:0] must access the aligned word given by its word index.
Any value of i_s_axi_awprot or i_s_axi_arprot must be accepted without error and without effect.
An unmapped access must not stall or change the state of the other channels.
The next transaction must behave as if the unmapped access had targeted a mapped address.
A valid input at 1 while i_rst_n is 0 must have no effect (REQ-RST-005).
Only 0x00 (REG_0) and 0x40 (STATUS) are mapped, o_regs is 32 bits wide, and 0x04 to 0x3C are unmapped.
0x00 to 0x3C are REG_0 to REG_15, 0x40 is STATUS, o_regs is 512 bits wide, and no address below 0x44 is unmapped.
The address space is 0x00 to 0x7F and addresses 0x44 to 0x7C are unmapped.
Every address with a 1 in any bit from 15 to 7 (e.g. 0x0080, 0x0100, 0x8040, 0xFFFC) is unmapped.
Latency, throughput, reset and back-pressure behaviour must be the same for every legal parameter combination.

not_verified.note: Cross-configuration equivalence; realised by running all timing/reset/back-pressure checks in every configuration of section 11.

statement: CFG-BASE uses PARA_NUM_REGS=8 and PARA_ADDR_W=8 as default and must cover the gap of unmapped addresses 0x20 to 0x3C.
CFG-MIN must be verified with PARA_NUM_REGS=1 and PARA_ADDR_W=7, the smallest legal configuration.
CFG-MAX must be verified with PARA_NUM_REGS=16 and PARA_ADDR_W=16, including aliasing checks with high address bits.
CFG-FULL-A7 uses PARA_NUM_REGS=16 and PARA_ADDR_W=7, a full register bank with the narrowest address bus and no unmapped address below 0x44.
The verification must run every configuration listed in the Configurations table (CFG-BASE, CFG-MIN, CFG-MAX, CFG-FULL-A7), as defined in run_set.json.

not_verified.note: Regression orchestration (run_set.json) over CFG-BASE, CFG-MIN, CFG-MAX, CFG-FULL-A7.

statement: The manager shall keep valid at 1 and its payload stable from the cycle it rises until the edge of its transfer.

not_verified.note: Manager obligation (REQ-VER-001); enforced as a stimulus constraint by all test drivers.

statement: The manager may hold i_s_axi_bready and i_s_axi_rready at 0 for any number of cycles, drive them at 1 before the matching valid, and make them depend on the valid.
The environment shall release i_rst_n synchronously to i_clk so that the release meets recovery and removal times of the flip-flops.

not_verified.note: Testbench obligation: i_rst_n released synchronously to i_clk in every test.

statement: The environment shall drive i_status synchronously to i_clk, changing it only away from rising edges.

not_verified.note: Testbench obligation: i_status changed only away from rising edges.

statement: The testbench shall drive defined values (no X or Z) on all inputs.

not_verified.note: Testbench obligation: all inputs driven to defined values while i_rst_n=1.

statement: The valids may be 0 or 1 during reset.
The environment shall drive i_rst_n = 0 from time zero, before the first rising edge of i_clk, for at least 2 cycles.
No output check applies, including REQ-VER-010, before the first assertion of i_rst_n, as outputs are undefined.

not_verified.note: Checker gating: all assertions are disabled until the first assertion of i_rst_n.

statement: A reset assertion ends the REQ-VER-001 obligation; the manager may drop that valid or change its payload.
A valid at 1 after R1 is a new request and carries the REQ-VER-001 obligation from that cycle.

not_verified.note: Manager obligation for valids after R1; stimulus constraint (exercised in CHK-036).

statement: A reference model shall predict o_regs and the next value of every handshake output.
The checker shall compare o_regs with the reference model in every cycle, not only after B transfers.
The checker shall compare o_s_axi_rdata and o_s_axi_rresp only when o_s_axi_rvalid is 1 or i_rst_n is 0, and o_s_axi_bresp only when o_s_axi_bvalid is 1 or i_rst_n is 0.
A protocol checker shall verify o_s_axi_bvalid and o_s_axi_rvalid stay 1 with stable payload until transfer, and no response code is 2'b01 or 2'b11.
The testbench shall change inputs between rising edges, e.g. at the falling edge, and check no output changes before the next rising edge.
The testbench shall assert i_rst_n between rising edges while transactions are in progress and check reset values before the next rising edge.
All 16 values of i_s_axi_wstrb shall be applied, with data differing from the old value in every byte.
Writes shall be run with address before data (gaps of 1 and 4+ cycles), data before address (same gaps), and both at the same edge.
The B channel shall be run with i_s_axi_bready delays of 0, 1 and 4 or more cycles, including i_s_axi_bready at 1 before o_s_axi_bvalid rises.
The R channel shall be run with i_s_axi_rready delays of 0, 1 and 4 or more cycles, including i_s_axi_rready at 1 before o_s_axi_rvalid rises.
New AW, W and AR valids shall be presented to check they are not taken (REQ-TIM-010, REQ-TIM-011).
Every mapped register shall be written with a unique value and read back to detect decode aliasing.
The status register shall be read while i_status changes around Ear and during R back-pressure, and written with several strobe values.
Unmapped addresses shall be accessed: word indexes PARA_NUM_REGS to 15, 0x44, the highest bus address, and mapped address plus a 1 in bit 7 to PARA_ADDR_W-1 when PARA_ADDR_W > 7.
Addresses with bits [1:0] not 2'b00 and random i_s_axi_awprot and i_s_axi_arprot values shall be applied.
A read and a write of the same register shall run with Ear at Ec-1, Ec and Ec+1, and reads and writes of different registers shall run simultaneously.
Reset shall be asserted with only write address held, only write data held, B response pending, R response pending, and with valids held at 1 through reset.
Back-to-back writes and reads at full throughput of REQ-TIM-001 and REQ-TIM-002 shall be run, alone and at the same time.
The block shall meet timing at 50 MHz (20 ns clock period) in the GF180MCU technology at the worst-case corner of the sign-off flow.

not_verified.note: Timing closure at 50 MHz in GF180MCU: STA.

statement: The RTL shall follow the coding rules in docs/RTL_RULES.md (REF-002).

not_verified.note: Coding rules: RTL review/lint.

statement: The RTL shall be synthesizable.

not_verified.note: Synthesizability: synthesis flow.

statement: The RTL shall use the single clock i_clk with no clock gating and no latches.

not_verified.note: Single clock, no gating, no latches: lint/synthesis.

statement: The RTL shall not rely on initial values.

not_verified.note: No reliance on initial values: lint/review.

statement: Every flip-flop that drives an output or holds transaction state shall be reset asynchronously by i_rst_n to the value giving the reset values of section 5.
Every output shall be driven directly from a flip-flop.

not_verified.note: Outputs driven from flip-flops is structural; observable effect checked by CHK-017 and CHK-037.

statement: The RTL shall compile and simulate in Verilator without lint warnings in all configurations of section 11.

not_verified.note: Verilator lint-clean in all configurations.

statement: The block should use no more storage than PARA_NUM_REGS x 32 register bits plus flip-flops for held write address and data, read data, and handshake state.

not_verified.note: Storage budget advice; not observable at interface.

statement: o_s_axi_awready, o_s_axi_wready and o_s_axi_arready must be 0 during reset and in the cycle that ends at R1, and 1 from R1.
The readies must be registered and depend only on the held state, not on the valids.
bvalid must be 1 from Ec, giving a write response latency of exactly 1 cycle.
rvalid must be 1 from Ear, giving a read data latency of exactly 1 cycle.
The register must be written at Ec, the later of the AW and W transfers.
The read must sample the register at Ear: a write at the same edge gives the old value, a write at an earlier Ec gives the new value.
i_status must be sampled at Ear and the sampled value held until Er.
Address bits [PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] must be fully decoded; any 1 above bit 6 makes the address unmapped.
bresp, rresp and rdata must be 0 during reset; their values while valid is 0 outside reset are not specified or checked.
The readies must return to 1 in the cycle after the B or R transfer, with no combinational path from bready or rready.
The RTL should stop elaboration with an error on illegal parameter values.

not_verified.note: Elaboration error on illegal parameters; not verified per REQ-PAR-004.

statement: A reset must end every held state; "after R1" means the most recent R1.
Reset must be applied from time zero for at least 2 cycles; outputs are undefined and unchecked before the first reset.
Reset ends the obligation on a pending request; a valid after R1 must be treated as a new request.
